newsitem.title: UK: C&W fends off talk about HK Telecom stake.
newsitem.headline: C&W fends off talk about HK Telecom stake.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Plc on Wednesday fended off market talk that Chinese interests might take a stake in its 58.5 percent-owned HK Telecommunications Ltd unit, saying it would be business as usual through the handover to Chinese rule.

"Hongkong Telecom is a successful and growing business and China is an important and fast-growing market. Everyone is seeking a very smooth transition (to Chinese rule)," said C&W spokeswoman Jennifer Weller.

"C&W will always act commercially and in the best interests of shareholders and customers. We are not compelled to do anything, neither do we make predictions about market-sensitive issues. We expect to be doing business as usual following the handover," Weller said.
Earlier, shares in Cable and Wireless rose on the back of gains in HK Telecom, amid talk that C&W's 58.5-percent owned HK unit is seeking a mainland Chinese investor, dealers said.
C&W shares were up 14-1/2p at 496-1/2 by 1516 GMT in volume of just over five million shares.
Dealers said talk of a Chinese investor in HK Telecom was not new but had resurfaced ahead of the end of British rule in the territory in July.
In Hong Kong, HK Telecom on Wednesday rose 10 HK cents to $HK14.20.
